title: What really matters at the end of life
speaker: BJ Miller

sentences.en: Well, we all need a reason to wake up. For me, it just took 11,000 volts.
sentences.zh: 我们都需要一个醒过来的理由 对我来说,它只是花了11000伏特。

sentences.en: I know you're too polite to ask, so I will tell you.
sentences.zh: 我知道你太礼貌了 不敢问 所以我会告诉你

sentences.en: One night, sophomore year of college, just back from Thanksgiving holiday, a few of my friends and I were horsing around, and we decided to climb atop a parked commuter train.
sentences.zh: 有一天晚上,大学二年级, 刚从感恩节回来, 我的一些朋友和我 到处奔波, 我们决定爬上 一辆停在车边的通勤列车。

sentences.en: It was just sitting there, with the wires that run overhead.
sentences.zh: 它只是坐在那里, 与电线运行上面。

sentences.en: Somehow, that seemed like a great idea at the time.
sentences.zh: 不知怎的,这似乎 一个伟大的想法在当时。

sentences.en: We'd certainly done stupider things. I scurried up the ladder on the back, and when I stood up, the electrical current entered my arm, blew down and out my feet, and that was that.
sentences.zh: 我们确实做了更蠢的事情。我把梯子往后爬, 当我站起来时,电流进入我的手臂, 炸掉我的脚,就这样了。

sentences.en: Would you believe that watch still works?
sentences.zh: 你相信这表还能用吗?

sentences.en: Takes a licking! (Laughter) My father wears it now in solidarity.
sentences.zh: 我父亲现在要团结地戴它

sentences.en: That night began my formal relationship with death -- my death -- and it also began my long run as a patient.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上,我开始正式的关系 与死亡,我的死亡, 它也开始我作为一个病人的长期运行。

sentences.en: It's a good word. It means one who suffers.
sentences.zh: 是个好词 意思是受苦的人

sentences.en: So I guess we're all patients. Now, the American health care system has more than its fair share of dysfunction -- to match its brilliance, to be sure.
sentences.zh: 所以,我想我们都是病人。现在,美国医疗体系的功能失调 不仅仅是与其聪明相匹配。

sentences.en: I'm a physician now, a hospice and palliative medicine doc, so I've seen care from both sides.
sentences.zh: 我现在是医生了 疗养院和疗养院的医生 所以我从两边都看到了治疗

sentences.en: And believe me: almost everyone who goes into healthcare really means well -- I mean, truly.
sentences.zh: 相信我,几乎每个人都去 医疗真的意味着很好,我的意思是,真的。

sentences.en: But we who work in it are also unwitting agents for a system that too often does not serve.
sentences.zh: 但是,我们在这个系统中工作的人,对于一个常常不能发挥作用的系统来说,也是不知情的代理人。

sentences.en: Why? Well, there's actually a pretty easy answer to that question, and it explains a lot: because healthcare was designed with diseases, not people, at its center.
sentences.zh: 为什么?事实上,这个问题的答案很简单, 它解释了很多: 因为医疗是用疾病设计的, 而不是人,在它的中心。

sentences.en: Which is to say, of course, it was badly designed.
sentences.zh: 也就是说,当然,它设计得很差

sentences.en: And nowhere are the effects of bad design more heartbreaking or the opportunity for good design more compelling than at the end of life, where things are so distilled and concentrated.
sentences.zh: 没有什么地方 坏设计的影响 更令人心碎 或机会 良好的设计 比在生命的末期, 在那里的东西 如此蒸馏和集中。

sentences.en: There are no do-overs. My purpose today is to reach out across disciplines and invite design thinking into this big conversation.
sentences.zh: 今天我的目标是跨学科的接触 并且邀请设计思维参与这次大型对话。

sentences.en: That is, to bring intention and creativity to the experience of dying.
sentences.zh: 也就是说,给死亡的经历带来意图和创造力。

sentences.en: We have a monumental opportunity in front of us, before one of the few universal issues as individuals as well as a civil society: to rethink and redesign how it is we die.
sentences.zh: 在我们面前,在作为个人和民间社会的少数普遍问题之一面前,我们有一个巨大的机会:重新思考和重新设计我们如何死去。

sentences.en: So let's begin at the end. For most people, the scariest thing about death isn't being dead, it's dying, suffering.
sentences.zh: 所以,让我们从最后开始。对大多数人来说, 最可怕的是死亡不是死亡,而是死亡,痛苦。

sentences.en: It's a key distinction. To get underneath this, it can be very helpful to tease out suffering which is necessary as it is, from suffering we can change.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关键的区别。要进入这个底部, 取笑痛苦是非常有帮助的,这是必要的, 从痛苦我们可以改变。

sentences.en: The former is a natural, essential part of life, part of the deal, and to this we are called to make space, adjust, grow.
sentences.zh: 前者是生命的自然重要部分 也是交易的一部分,为此,我们被要求创造空间,调整,成长。

sentences.en: It can be really good to realize forces larger than ourselves.
sentences.zh: 发现比我们大的力量是非常好的。

sentences.en: They bring proportionality, like a cosmic right-sizing.
sentences.zh: 它们带来相称性, 就像宇宙右侧的分级。

sentences.en: After my limbs were gone, that loss, for example, became fact, fixed -- necessarily part of my life, and I learned that I could no more reject this fact than reject myself.
sentences.zh: 在我四肢消失之后,比如说,失去的东西变成了事实,固定了 -- -- 必然是我生命的一部分,我学会了,我不能拒绝这个事实,而只能拒绝自己。

sentences.en: It took me a while, but I learned it eventually.
sentences.zh: 花了我一阵子 但我终于学会了

sentences.en: Now, another great thing about necessary suffering is that it is the very thing that unites caregiver and care receiver -- human beings.
sentences.zh: 现在,关于必要痛苦的另一件伟大的事情是,它正是把护理者和护理接受者 -- -- 人类 -- -- 联系在一起的。

sentences.en: This, we are finally realizing, is where healing happens.
sentences.zh: 这,我们终于意识到, 是哪里可以治愈。

sentences.en: Yes, compassion -- literally, as we learned yesterday -- suffering together.
sentences.zh: 是的,同情 -- -- 正如我们昨天学到的那样 -- -- 一起受苦受难。

sentences.en: Now, on the systems side, on the other hand, so much of the suffering is unnecessary, invented.
sentences.zh: 现在,在系统方面, 另一方面, 这么多的痛苦是不必要的, 发明的。

sentences.en: It serves no good purpose. But the good news is, since this brand of suffering is made up, well, we can change it.
sentences.zh: 但好消息是,既然这种痛苦是编造的,我们可以改变它。

sentences.en: How we die is indeed something we can affect.
sentences.zh: 我们如何死去确实是我们能影响的东西。

sentences.en: Making the system sensitive to this fundamental distinction between necessary and unnecessary suffering gives us our first of three design cues for the day.
sentences.zh: 使这个系统对必要和不必要痛苦之间的这一根本区别具有敏感性,这为我们提供了今天三个设计提示中的第一个。

sentences.en: After all, our role as caregivers, as people who care, is to relieve suffering -- not add to the pile.
sentences.zh: 毕竟,我们作为照顾者,作为关心者的作用是减轻痛苦 -- -- 而不是增加负担。

sentences.en: True to the tenets of palliative care, I function as something of a reflective advocate, as much as prescribing physician.
sentences.zh: 忠于姑息治疗的原则, 我作为一个反思的倡导者, 就像开处方的医生。

sentences.en: Quick aside: palliative care -- a very important field but poorly understood -- while it includes, it is not limited to end of life care.
sentences.zh: 简而言之,姑息治疗 -- -- 一个重要的领域,但人们不甚了解 -- -- 虽然它包括,但它并不限于临终护理。

sentences.en: It is not limited to hospice. It's simply about comfort and living well at any stage.
sentences.zh: 它不仅限于疗养院,它只是关于舒适和在任何阶段都过好日子。

sentences.en: So please know that you don't have to be dying anytime soon to benefit from palliative care.
sentences.zh: 所以,请知道,你不必死 很快从姑息治疗。

sentences.en: Now, let me introduce you to Frank. Sort of makes this point.
sentences.zh: 现在,我给你介绍弗兰克 有点意思

sentences.en: I've been seeing Frank now for years. He's living with advancing prostate cancer on top of long-standing HIV.
sentences.zh: 我和弗兰克交往了好几年了 他除了长期感染艾滋病外 还患有前列腺癌

sentences.en: We work on his bone pain and his fatigue, but most of the time we spend thinking out loud together about his life -- really, about our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们研究他的骨痛和疲劳, 但是大部分时间我们一起 大声地思考他的生活-- 真的,关于我们的生活。

sentences.en: In this way, Frank grieves. In this way, he keeps up with his losses as they roll in, so that he's ready to take in the next moment.
sentences.zh: 这样,弗兰克会伤心的,这样,他继续承受损失, 这样他就可以在接下来的时刻接受。

sentences.en: Loss is one thing, but regret, quite another.
sentences.zh: 失去是一回事 但后悔是另一回事

sentences.en: Frank has always been an adventurer -- he looks like something out of a Norman Rockwell painting -- and no fan of regret.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克一直都是个冒险家 他看起来像是诺曼·洛克威尔画的画一样 没有遗憾的粉丝

sentences.en: So it wasn't surprising when he came into clinic one day, saying he wanted to raft down the Colorado River.
sentences.zh: 有一天他来到诊所 说想从科罗拉多河下岸 这并不奇怪

sentences.en: Was this a good idea? With all the risks to his safety and his health, some would say no.
sentences.zh: 这是个好主意吗?

sentences.en: Many did, but he went for it, while he still could.
sentences.zh: 很多人都这么做了,但是他去,虽然他仍然可以。

sentences.en: It was a glorious, marvelous trip: freezing water, blistering dry heat, scorpions, snakes, wildlife howling off the flaming walls of the Grand Canyon --
sentences.zh: 这是一次光辉而奇妙的旅行: 冷水,潮湿的干热, 蝎子,蛇,野生生物 咆哮在大峡谷的燃烧的墙上 --

sentences.en: all the glorious side of the world beyond our control.
sentences.zh: 我们无法控制的世界的光荣一面

sentences.en: Frank's decision, while maybe dramatic, is exactly the kind so many of us would make, if we only had the support to figure out what is best for ourselves over time.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克的决定,或许是戏剧性的, 恰恰是我们很多人会做的那种, 如果我们只是得到支持 来找出什么是最好的 时间。

sentences.en: So much of what we're talking about today is a shift in perspective.
sentences.zh: 我们今天谈论的 大部分是观点的转变

sentences.en: After my accident, when I went back to college, I changed my major to art history.
sentences.zh: 事故发生后,我回到大学时, 我改变了我的专业 艺术史。

sentences.en: Studying visual art, I figured I'd learn something about how to see -- a really potent lesson for a kid who couldn't change so much of what he was seeing.
sentences.zh: 研究视觉艺术,我想我会学到一些关于如何看的东西-- 一个对一个无法改变自己所看到的东西的孩子来说非常有力的教训。

sentences.en: Perspective, that kind of alchemy we humans get to play with, turning anguish into a flower.
sentences.zh: 透视,那种我们人类可以玩的炼金术 将痛苦变成一朵花

sentences.en: Flash forward: now I work at an amazing place in San Francisco called the Zen Hospice Project, where we have a little ritual that helps with this shift in perspective.
sentences.zh: 向前看:现在我在旧金山一个叫"Zen Hospice项目"的地方工作, 在那里我们有一个小小的仪式 来帮助这种观点的转变。

sentences.en: When one of our residents dies, the mortuary men come, and as we're wheeling the body out through the garden, heading for the gate, we pause.
sentences.zh: 当我们的一个居民死了,停尸房的人来了, 当我们把尸体从花园里运出去, 朝大门走去,我们暂停。

sentences.en: Anyone who wants -- fellow residents, family, nurses, volunteers, the hearse drivers too, now -- shares a story or a song or silence, as we sprinkle the body with flower petals.
sentences.zh: 任何想要的人 -- -- 居民同胞、家人、护士、志愿者、灵车司机 -- -- 现在都分享一个故事或一首歌或沉默,因为我们用花瓣洒在身体上。

sentences.en: It takes a few minutes; it's a sweet, simple parting image to usher in grief with warmth, rather than repugnance.
sentences.zh: 它需要几分钟; 它是一个甜蜜的,简单的分离图像 带来悲伤 温暖,而不是令人厌恶。

sentences.en: Contrast that with the typical experience in the hospital setting, much like this -- floodlit room lined with tubes and beeping machines and blinking lights that don't stop even when the patient's life has.
sentences.zh: 对比一下医院环境的典型经验, 像这样-- 洪流室里装有管子和蜂鸣机, 闪烁着灯光, 即使病人的生命也无法停止。

sentences.en: Cleaning crew swoops in, the body's whisked away, and it all feels as though that person had never really existed.
sentences.zh: 清理人员冲进来 尸体被冲走 感觉好像那人从未真正存在过

sentences.en: Well-intended, of course, in the name of sterility, but hospitals tend to assault our senses, and the most we might hope for within those walls is numbness -- anesthetic, literally the opposite of aesthetic.
sentences.zh: 当然,用不育的名声来表达, 但是医院往往会攻击我们的感官, 我们最希望的就是那些墙壁里的麻木 -- 麻醉, 与美学完全相反。

sentences.en: I revere hospitals for what they can do; I am alive because of them.
sentences.zh: 我敬重医院的本能;我之所以活着是因为医院。

sentences.en: But we ask too much of our hospitals. They are places for acute trauma and treatable illness.
sentences.zh: 但是,我们要求的医院太多,它们是严重创伤和可治疗疾病的场所。

sentences.en: They are no place to live and die; that's not what they were designed for.
sentences.zh: 它们不是生死之地,它们不是设计用来生存的。

sentences.en: Now mind you -- I am not giving up on the notion that our institutions can become more humane.
sentences.zh: 现在请记住 -- -- 我不会放弃我们的机构可以变得更人道的观念。

sentences.en: Beauty can be found anywhere. I spent a few months in a burn unit at St. Barnabas Hospital in Livingston, New Jersey, where I got really great care at every turn,
sentences.zh: 我在新泽西利文斯顿的圣巴纳巴斯医院的烧伤病房待了几个月

sentences.en: including good palliative care for my pain.
sentences.zh: 包括良好的缓解治疗我的痛苦。

sentences.en: And one night, it began to snow outside.
sentences.zh: 一天晚上 外面开始下雪

sentences.en: I remember my nurses complaining about driving through it.
sentences.zh: 我记得我的护士 抱怨开车通过它。

sentences.en: And there was no window in my room, but it was great to just imagine it coming down all sticky.
sentences.zh: 我的房间没有窗户, 但是它只是 想象下来所有的粘粘。

sentences.en: Next day, one of my nurses smuggled in a snowball for me.
sentences.zh: 第二天,我的一个护士 走私在雪球我。

sentences.en: She brought it in to the unit. I cannot tell you the rapture I felt holding that in my hand, and the coldness dripping onto my burning skin; the miracle of it all,
sentences.zh: 她把它带到了单位。我无法告诉你,我手里握着那股欢乐,寒冷滴到我燃烧的皮肤上,一切奇迹,

sentences.en: the fascination as I watched it melt and turn into water.
sentences.zh: 我看着它融化 变成水时的魅力

sentences.en: In that moment, just being any part of this planet in this universe mattered more to me than whether I lived or died.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻,只是成为这个星球的任何一部分 在这个宇宙中,我比 我生还是死更重要。

sentences.en: That little snowball packed all the inspiration I needed to both try to live and be OK if I did not.
sentences.zh: 那个小雪球 装满了所有我需要的灵感 试图生活 如果我不活着,就没事。

sentences.en: In a hospital, that's a stolen moment. In my work over the years, I've known many people who were ready to go, ready to die.
sentences.zh: 在一个医院里,那是个偷来的瞬间。在我多年的工作里, 我认识很多人准备去,准备去死。

sentences.en: Not because they had found some final peace or transcendence, but because they were so repulsed by what their lives had become -- in a word, cut off, or ugly.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为他们找到了最后的和平或超越,而是因为他们的生活变得如此令人厌恶 -- -- 一句话说,是被切断的还是丑陋的。

sentences.en: There are already record numbers of us living with chronic and terminal illness, and into ever older age.
sentences.zh: 我们已经有创纪录的数字 生活在慢性和终期疾病, 并进入越来越老的年纪。

sentences.en: And we are nowhere near ready or prepared for this silver tsunami.
sentences.zh: 我们还没准备好 也没有准备好迎接这场银色海啸

sentences.en: We need an infrastructure dynamic enough to handle these seismic shifts in our population.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一个足够活跃的基础设施来应对我们人口的这些地震变化。

sentences.en: Now is the time to create something new, something vital.
sentences.zh: 现在是创造新东西的时候了 重要的东西

sentences.en: I know we can because we have to. The alternative is just unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们能做到,因为我们必须这样做 选择是无法接受的

sentences.en: And the key ingredients are known: policy, education and training, systems, bricks and mortar.
sentences.zh: 关键成分是众所周知的:政策、教育和培训、系统、砖块和迫击炮。

sentences.en: We have tons of input for designers of all stripes to work with.
sentences.zh: 我们有成吨的输入 设计师的所有条纹 工作。

sentences.en: We know, for example, from research what's most important to people who are closer to death: comfort; feeling unburdened and unburdening to those they love;
sentences.zh: 例如,我们从研究中知道,对于更接近死亡的人来说,什么是最重要的:舒适;对他们所爱的人感到无负担和无负担;

sentences.en: existential peace; and a sense of wonderment and spirituality.
sentences.zh: 生存的和平;以及一种奇观和精神感。

sentences.en: Over Zen Hospice's nearly 30 years, we've learned much more from our residents in subtle detail.
sentences.zh: 在Zen Hospice近30年的时间里, 我们从我们的居民那里学到了更多细节。

sentences.en: Little things aren't so little. Take Janette.
sentences.zh: 小东西没那么小 带上珍妮特

sentences.en: She finds it harder to breathe one day to the next due to ALS.
sentences.zh: 她发现呼吸困难 一天到第二天,因为ALS。

sentences.en: Well, guess what? She wants to start smoking again -- and French cigarettes, if you please.
sentences.zh: 好吧,你猜怎么着,她又想抽烟了,还有法国香烟,如果你愿意的话

sentences.en: Not out of some self-destructive bent, but to feel her lungs filled while she has them.
sentences.zh: 不是从自我毁灭的弯曲, 而是在她有肺的时候感觉到她的肺充斥。

sentences.en: Priorities change. Or Kate -- she just wants to know her dog Austin is lying at the foot of her bed, his cold muzzle against her dry skin,
sentences.zh: 或者凯特 她只是想知道她的狗奥斯汀躺在床脚上

sentences.en: instead of more chemotherapy coursing through her veins -- she's done that.
sentences.zh: 而不是更多的化疗 在她的血管中循环—— 她做到了。

sentences.en: Sensuous, aesthetic gratification, where in a moment, in an instant, we are rewarded for just being.
sentences.zh: 敏锐 美感满足 瞬间 我们因刚出现而得到奖励

sentences.en: So much of it comes down to loving our time by way of the senses, by way of the body -- the very thing doing the living and the dying.
sentences.zh: 大部分都归结于 爱我们的时间 通过感官, 通过身体-- 就是做活和死的东西。

sentences.en: Probably the most poignant room in the Zen Hospice guest house is our kitchen, which is a little strange when you realize that so many of our residents can eat very little, if anything at all.
sentences.zh: 可能是Zen Hospice客房里最有吸引力的房间 就是我们的厨房 有点奇怪 当你意识到我们很多居民 都吃得很少的时候

sentences.en: But we realize we are providing sustenance on several levels: smell, a symbolic plane.
sentences.zh: 但是,我们意识到,我们正在提供几个层面的生计:嗅觉,象征性的平面。

sentences.en: Seriously, with all the heavy-duty stuff happening under our roof, one of the most tried and true interventions we know of, is to bake cookies.
sentences.zh: 说真的,我们屋檐下发生了很多重担的事情, 最努力和真正的干预之一, 就是烤饼干。

sentences.en: As long as we have our senses -- even just one -- we have at least the possibility of accessing what makes us feel human, connected.
sentences.zh: 只要我们有知觉 -- -- 甚至只有一种知觉 -- -- 我们至少有机会接触使我们感到人性、相互联系的东西。

sentences.en: Imagine the ripples of this notion for the millions of people living and dying with dementia.
sentences.zh: 想象一下这个概念对数百万患有痴呆症的人的连锁反应

sentences.en: Primal sensorial delights that say the things we don't have words for, impulses that make us stay present -- no need for a past or a future.
sentences.zh: 原始感官喜悦 说那些我们没有语言表达的东西 和让我们保持现状的冲动 不需要过去或未来

sentences.en: So, if teasing unnecessary suffering out of the system was our first design cue, then tending to dignity by way of the senses, by way of the body -- the aesthetic realm --
sentences.zh: 所以,如果取笑不必要的痛苦 出系统是我们的第一个设计提示, 然后通过感官, 通过身体-- 美学界 --

sentences.en: is design cue number two. Now this gets us quickly to the third and final bit for today; namely, we need to lift our sights, to set our sights on well-being,
sentences.zh: 这是第二个设计提示。现在这让我们很快地到达今天的第三个也是最后一个点, 也就是说,我们需要提高我们的视野, 使我们的目光着眼于福祉,

sentences.en: so that life and health and healthcare can become about making life more wonderful, rather than just less horrible.
sentences.zh: 这样,生命和健康 和保健可以变成 使生活更加美好, 而不是只是更少的恐怖。

sentences.en: Beneficence. Here, this gets right at the distinction between a disease-centered and a patient- or human-centered model of care, and here is where caring becomes a creative, generative,
sentences.zh: 好处。在这里,这得到了正确的区别 以疾病为中心 和以病人或人为中心 护理模式,

sentences.en: even playful act. "Play" may sound like a funny word here.
sentences.zh: "打球"可能听起来像一个有趣的词

sentences.en: But it is also one of our highest forms of adaptation.
sentences.zh: 但它也是我们最高适应形式之一。

sentences.en: Consider every major compulsory effort it takes to be human.
sentences.zh: 想想所有必要的重大努力都是人类的

sentences.en: The need for food has birthed cuisine. The need for shelter has given rise to architecture.
sentences.zh: 食物需求产生了烹饪,住房需求产生了建筑。

sentences.en: The need for cover, fashion. And for being subjected to the clock, well, we invented music.
sentences.zh: 需要伪装 时尚 需要时间

sentences.en: So, since dying is a necessary part of life, what might we create with this fact?
sentences.zh: 所以,既然死亡是生命的必要部分, 我们用这个事实来创造什么呢?

sentences.en: By "play" I am in no way suggesting we take a light approach to dying or that we mandate any particular way of dying.
sentences.zh: 使用“玩耍”我绝不是建议我们对死亡采取轻视的态度,或者我们授权任何特定的死亡方式。

sentences.en: There are mountains of sorrow that cannot move, and one way or another, we will all kneel there.
sentences.zh: 有很多悲伤的山 无法移动, 和任何一种方式, 我们都会跪在那里。

sentences.en: Rather, I am asking that we make space -- physical, psychic room, to allow life to play itself all the way out -- so that rather than just getting out of the way,
sentences.zh: 相反,我要求我们创造空间 -- 物理的,精神的, 让生活可以玩 自己一路出去, 这样,而不是只是让路,

sentences.en: aging and dying can become a process of crescendo through to the end.
sentences.zh: 衰老和死亡 可能变成一个过程 弯曲到底。

sentences.en: We can't solve for death. I know some of you are working on this.
sentences.zh: 我们不能解决死亡问题 我知道你们中有些人正在研究这个

sentences.en: (Laughter) Meanwhile, we can -- (Laughter) We can design towards it.
sentences.zh: 同时,我们可以-- 我们可以设计它。

sentences.en: Parts of me died early on, and that's something we can all say one way or another.
sentences.zh: 我的一部分早死了, 这也是我们都可以说 一种或另一种方式。

sentences.en: I got to redesign my life around this fact, and I tell you it has been a liberation to realize you can always find a shock of beauty or meaning in what life you have left, like that snowball lasting for a perfect moment,
sentences.zh: 我必须重新设计我的生活围绕这个事实, 我告诉你,这是一个解放 意识到你总是可以发现 美的震撼或意义 在你留下的生活, 像雪球 持续一个完美的时刻,

sentences.en: all the while melting away. If we love such moments ferociously, then maybe we can learn to live well --
sentences.zh: 如果我们疯狂地爱这种时刻 也许我们可以学会过好日子

sentences.en: not in spite of death, but because of it.
sentences.zh: 不是因为死亡 而是因为死亡

sentences.en: Let death be what takes us, not lack of imagination.
sentences.zh: 让死亡成为需要我们的东西,而不是缺乏想象力。

sentences.en: Thank you. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 谢谢。 （掌声）
